scope: Expansion entries only. Existing 59 anthology records retained verbatim; the 1,098 dated Year entries were not re-audited.
method: Original texts, official franchise quotations and institutional archives checked for words, speaker, edition and setting. Supplementary evidence is labelled in each record. Trailer quotations are not assigned unverified episode locations. Research records are evidence; automated checks validate data and behaviour, not historical truth.
presentation: The established dawn and night palette, typography and cards remain. Each collection presents its new entries first. All old IDs and sources remain available.
daily: Today retains the dated Year reading plus nine unique excerpts spanning all six collections, stable within the chosen shift day. Existing library-only entries stay excluded.

trek-wars.scope: Seven new Star Trek and nine new Star Wars quotations. No app files changed by this researcher.
trek-wars.method: Exact wording, speaker, source work and scene checked against official franchise material, supplemented only where explicitly identified. These are brief quotations with new editorial context. No full episodes or films were streamed.
trek-wars.existingChecked: C:/Users/zpull/FirstLight/js/data-anthology.js; no duplicate id or text among 59 existing entries. New public source URLs do not reuse any of the existing anthology quote URLs.
trek-wars.wordBudgetPolicy: At most 25 quoted words per retrieved copyrighted source across the retained collection; duplicated source URLs normalised. Secondary links that only support location are conservatively counted with the full quote in this table.

entries.evidence: The official Get To Know character section prints the selected complete first sentence under Jean-Luc Picard. Paramount identifies Peak Performance as TNG S2E21 and dates it to 1989. The indexed production-script page 37A reproduces Picard's reassurance to Data in that episode.
entries.notes: The following sentence differs across official promotional transcription and circulating episode transcripts in its use of an article before weakness. It is deliberately not included. Production draft consulted through its indexed passage; no claim to have streamed the full episode.

entries.evidence: Article lines 78-82 introduce Sisko's explanation to the wormhole beings, reproduce the quoted sentence in full, and identify Emissary. The official premiere retrospective confirms 1993.
entries.notes: An uninterrupted complete sentence; not the article writer's paraphrased reprise near its conclusion.

entries.evidence: Official staff compilation lines 85-89 prints Kira's speech under By Inferno's Light and identifies her conversation with Ziyal in its image caption. Paramount episode record confirms 1997.
entries.notes: Final complete sentence of a longer speech, explicitly labelled as an excerpt.

entries.evidence: Official compilation lines 93-96 attributes the final sentence to Odo under A Man Alone, with the Commander's-office debate in the caption.
entries.notes: Episode numbering differs when the series pilot is counted as one or two parts; published locator uses the episode title, not an unstable number.

entries.evidence: Official video landing page lines 30-36 prints the full selected quotation and identifies Captain Janeway. Supplementary episode dialogue transcript locates it on the bridge in The Cloud after the discussion of an energy source.
entries.notes: The quotation itself is verified against official material. Scene locator is corroborated by a clearly labelled fan transcript; the linked official video was not streamed. Locator omits episode number because single/double pilot numbering varies.

entries.evidence: Official leadership article quotes Pike and explicitly names Memento Mori in the same paragraph. Paramount's official season listing dates the episode to May 2022.
entries.notes: Initial lowercase is retained from the official article's embedded quotation; locator marks an excerpt. Context is editorial interpretation of the depicted leadership.

entries.evidence: Official finale retrospective lines 41-43 reproduces Sisko's toast, identifies Vic's lounge and dates the finale to 2 June 1999.
entries.notes: Only the complete opening sentence is reproduced.

entries.evidence: Lucasfilm's A New Hope quotations article item 19 attributes the selected sentence to Leia and continues with the garbage-chute command. Its companion 40 memorable moments article explains Leia taking control of the rescue.
entries.notes: Only the opening complete sentence is included, not the whole command.

entries.evidence: Lucasfilm's everyday quotations article item 5 prints exact words, names Obi-Wan, and its image caption identifies him aboard the Falcon in A New Hope.
entries.notes: Punctuation follows the chosen source without the comma inserted by some other versions. Context separates the fictional Force from a factual claim about chance.

entries.evidence: Han's official Databank quote panel prints the selected words with exclamation point and labels The Empire Strikes Back. The official original-clip page corroborates the film and scene; the Empire at 40 article item 16 confirms the same words.
entries.notes: Video landing page and textual quote panel inspected, not the full movie or playback. An entertainment quotation about nerve is not presented as practical advice to ignore risk.

entries.evidence: Lucasfilm's Andor/Rogue One comparison section 6 states the quotation, identifies Jyn's Rebel council appeal, and explains her repetition of Cassian and the later prequel's Thela connection.
entries.notes: Attribution is Jyn for this particular film scene, not a claim that she originated the in-world wording or that Andor was released first.

entries.evidence: Official Time to Fly episode-guide Quotes section prints this sentence verbatim under Ahsoka Tano. Its official highlights page describes the resumed training of Sabine.
entries.notes: Dynamic open response omitted some quote cards; their complete official text was retrieved by the web search result for the same canonical episode-guide URL. This was not copied from a fan quotation site.

entries.evidence: The same official episode guide names Sabine Wren beside her exact quoted commitment.
entries.notes: Combined with the Ahsoka sentence, the source contributes 21 quoted words.

entries.evidence: Official April 2015 Hera feature identifies the conclusion of Vision of Hope and prints the selected first sentence. The episode guide confirms the title and the betrayal plot.
entries.notes: Official pages disagree about can versus will in the following sentence. Only the three-word sentence they agree on is retained. Article open timed out once, but full official text was recovered in targeted search.

entries.evidence: Official Rose Databank Quotes section prints all three selected short sentences and labels The Last Jedi. The same page describes Rose stopping Finn on Crait and speaking in the wreckage.
entries.notes: Preserves the official wording gonna and its sentence boundaries. Dynamic open returned biography without quote gallery, but the complete official quote panel was retrieved in web search for the same URL.

entries.evidence: Official Luke biography lines 168-170 describes his refusal to kill Vader and prints the selected quotation directly.
entries.notes: Uses I am, not the contraction often remembered. Scene and quotation are supported together in Lucasfilm's own biography.
